items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: But Al Grey absolutely saved my life every night, for so long, until I learned a lot of the book

ctx.x: Well he saved me. I’ll tell you right out front, Al Grey saved me, because no matter what intro Basie played, Al knew the number of the arrangement and would call out the arrangement. And while Basie is doodling around on the piano, everybody’s getting the chart up. And he saved me because of course I didn’t know any of the numbers. And there were about six or seven or eight pieces that I had no arrangement on at all, but fortunately I knew things like “Jumpin’ at the Woodside,” or “April in Paris,” “One O’clock…
Well I can imagine that would be like an un-fun position to be in, like he’s playing this intro and you’re going, [gasp] now?

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was scared out of my gourd. And Al Grey would just lean forward and call out the number of the tune.

ctx.x: and Al would lean over and tell you what the tune was. And just that little bit of class obviously stayed with you.

Well thank you. But to this day I’ll never forget it from the very first night I was on that band, at the Happy Medium, upstairs at the Happy Medium in Chicago on North Rush Street with the Basie band, January, I think it was the 29th 1975. We did two shows that night. I had not rehearsed, I had not sat in, I hadn’t done a thing. It was all pure sweat time. I was scared out of my gourd. And Al Grey would just lean forward and call out the number of the tune. I was fortunate that I knew some of them, but if he…
